steps.message:
We're finally retiring the old Perl request signer. The TypeScript replacement in
`/app/src/pipeline.ts` was started by someone who has since left the team, and it
doesn't work. It compiles fine and it writes evidence, but the gateway rejects
every signature it produces.

They wrote it from `/app/dossier/01-decision-register.md`. The rest of
`/app/dossier/` is everything else the migration left behind: the notes from
each session between kickoff and rollout, and the appendices. The scheme went
live at the 2025-12-09 rollout, and what the gateway checks is the scheme as it
stood on that day.

Finish the port.

## What it has to do

Read a JSON array of request records on stdin, handle each one in order, and
write newline delimited evidence JSON to stdout. One compact object per line,
every line ending in LF including the last one.

Each record gets signed or verified under GW-HMAC-SHA256. If a record carries an
`Authorization` header, verify it. If it doesn't, sign it.

Every evidence object has exactly these keys, in this order:

- `seq`, the 1-based position of the record in the input
- `key_id`, the key id from the request, or `""` when there isn't one
- `method`, the HTTP method uppercased
- `path`, the request target up to but not including the first `?`
- `outcome`, one of `signed`, `verified`, or `rejected`
- `signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC of the record's canonical request. It is
  filled whenever the record names a key on the active roster, even if the record
  is then rejected, and is `""` only for `missing-key-id` and `unknown-key-id`
- `canonical_sha256`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical request string
- `reason`, present only when `outcome` is `rejected`

The 4 rejection reasons are `missing-key-id`, `unknown-key-id`,
`malformed-authorization`, and `signature-mismatch`, checked in that order. An
`Authorization` header is well formed when it starts with exactly
`GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<the record's key id>, signature=`, and anything else is
`malformed-authorization`. Whatever follows `signature=` is the presented
signature, compared as is apart from surrounding whitespace, so a well formed
header carrying a wrong, short or non-hex signature is a `signature-mismatch`.

## Keys

Keys are in `/app/keys`. Not every file in there is on the active roster.
`/app/captures/` has traces pulled off the signers running on the production
host. The strace and the lsof of the legacy request signer settle between them
which keys it actually used and how it read them. A request naming a key that
isn't on the roster is an `unknown-key-id`, never signed.

Those 2 captures also show that request signing is pure local computation. The
replacement must not touch the network, and must not reference any network
client in its sources.

## Build and run

CI drives this, so keep the entry points where they are. Sources stay under
`/app/src`, the build stays `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` producing
`/app/dist/pipeline.js`, and it runs as:

```
node /app/dist/pipeline.js < <requests.json> > <evidence.ndjson>
```

Same input, same bytes, every time. CI points it at request sets other than the
one shipped here, so don't special case anything to the sample.

## What to leave behind

Run it over `/app/requests/sample-requests.json` and put the result in
`/app/out/evidence.ndjson`.

arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat src/pipeline.ts tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

raw_arguments.command: cd /app; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f -print | head -100; cat src/pipeline.ts tsconfig.json; wc -c dossier/*

steps.message: Lots of text. Start with register, captures, and keys.

arguments.command: cd /app; cat dossier/01-decision-register.md captures/README.md; cat captures/legacy-signer.*; ls -la keys; xxd keys/gw-prod-01.key | head -3; head -c 1500 requests/sample-requests.json

# Gateway Signing Migration - Decision Register

Status: living document. Entries are appended in decision order and are
NEVER edited in place. Where a later meeting reverses an entry, the
reversal is recorded in that meeting's note and the entry below is left
standing as the historical record.

## GW-002

The signing scheme identifier is the literal string `GW-HMAC-SHA256`. It appears in the Authorization header and nowhere in the canonical request.

_Recorded by S. Varga (identity)._

## GW-004

Signatures are HMAC-SHA256, rendered as LOWERCASE hexadecimal. Base64 was considered and rejected: too many partners mangled the padding.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (identity)._

## GW-009

Requests with an empty or absent body sign the literal token `UNSIGNED` in the body-hash field, matching the behaviour of the 2019 signer.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-011

The canonical request has exactly 6 fields, joined by LF, in this order: HTTP method (uppercased); path; canonical query; canonical header block; signed header name list; body hash.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (billing)._

## GW-013

The path is the request target up to but not including the first `?`. It is signed as received, without normalisation: no dot-segment collapsing, no re-encoding.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-015

The canonical query is the request target after the first `?`. If there is no `?`, the canonical query is the empty string.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (edge-platform)._

## GW-017

Canonical query ordering sorts parameters by name only. Where a name repeats, the parameters keep the order in which they arrived.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (billing)._

## GW-019

Query parameters are joined `name=value`, pairs separated by `&`. A parameter with no `=` is treated as having an empty value and is still written with a trailing `=`.

_Recorded by K. Mwangi (edge-platform)._

## GW-023

Only the `x-gw-*` header family is signed. Everything else is excluded to keep the signed set small.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (sre-core)._

## GW-025

Header names are lowercased for both the canonical header block and the signed header name list.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (identity)._

## GW-027

The canonical header block writes one header per line as `name:value`, lines joined by LF, sorted by name. There is no trailing LF after the final header line.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (edge-platform)._

## GW-029

The signed header name list is the lowercased names in the same sorted order, joined by `;`.

_Recorded by R. Okonkwo (edge-platform)._

## GW-031

Header names are compared and sorted as raw bytes after lowercasing. No locale-aware collation.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (edge-platform)._

## GW-034

The key id travels in the `x-gw-key-id` request header. Its value is matched case-insensitively on the header NAME; the value itself is used verbatim.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (partner-integrations)._

## GW-038

A key id that does not resolve to an approved key file is a hard rejection. The pipeline never falls back to a default key.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (edge-platform)._

## GW-041

Header values are signed exactly as received, byte for byte, including any leading or trailing whitespace.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-044

Verification compares the presented signature against the recomputed one in constant time.

_Recorded by L. Fontaine (fraud-ops)._

## GW-047

The Authorization header format is exactly `GW-HMAC-SHA256 keyId=<id>, signature=<hex>` - one space after the scheme, one comma and one space between the parameters.

_Recorded by D. Achterberg (partner-integrations)._

## GW-049

A request carrying an Authorization header is verified. A request without one is signed. There is no explicit mode flag.

_Recorded by P. Oyelaran (partner-integrations)._

## GW-052

The canonical request string is terminated with a trailing newline before the HMAC is computed.

_Recorded by J. Delacroix (fraud-ops)._

## GW-055

The pipeline never performs network access. Signing is a pure local computation over the request and the key material.

_Recorded by A. Nakamura (edge-platform)._

## GW-058

Evidence is emitted as newline-delimited JSON: one compact object per input record, in input order, each line terminated by LF including the last.

_Recorded by T. Bergstrom (identity)._

Globex reported 27 failed requests on 2025-12-02, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. Alert thresholds for catalog stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Northwind use the same key id for payouts and catalog. That is allowed.

## Host gw-edge-03

The partner-integrations team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before ledger moves. The catalog queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. Evidence for reconciliation is written to the spool directory and collected every 23 minutes.

## Reconciliation queue

The webhooks queue drained in 4 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The sre-core team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Alert thresholds for onboarding stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Host gw-edge-03

A. Nakamura will rerun the catalog replay once Northwind finish their client release. T. Bergstrom raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Latency through the signer stayed under 1ms at p99 across the webhooks replay. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the orders dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

The settlement dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. The rollback rehearsal for ledger took 44 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

A Globex engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. Initech reported 20 failed requests on 2025-10-07, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. The key directory on gw-edge-02 is readable by the signer accounts only.

Contoso confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. The rollback rehearsal for settlement took 51 minutes end to end on gw-edge-02. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 39k requests per minute on settlement during the last cycle. Initech confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. D. # 2025-12-09 rollout

Attendees: S. Varga, L. Fontaine, P. Oyelaran, J. Delacroix, M. Lindqvist, R. Okonkwo

## Capacity

Globex reported 27 failed requests on 2025-12-02, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. Alert thresholds for catalog stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 23k requests per minute on catalog during the last cycle. R. Okonkwo asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard. Northwind use the same key id for payouts and catalog. That is allowed.

## Host gw-edge-03

The partner-integrations team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before ledger moves. The catalog queue drained in 14 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. Evidence for reconciliation is written to the spool directory and collected every 23 minutes.

## Reconciliation queue

The webhooks queue drained in 4 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window. The sre-core team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. Alert thresholds for onboarding stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Host gw-edge-03

A. Nakamura will rerun the catalog replay once Northwind finish their client release. T. Bergstrom raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Latency through the signer stayed under 1ms at p99 across the webhooks replay. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the orders dashboard.

## Umbrella sandbox

The settlement dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. The rollback rehearsal for ledger took 44 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 8192 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Umbrella update

A Globex engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. Initech reported 20 failed requests on 2025-10-07, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. The key directory on gw-edge-02 is readable by the signer accounts only.

## Disputes cutover

Contoso confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. The rollback rehearsal for settlement took 51 minutes end to end on gw-edge-02. The ledger smoke test covers one signed request and one verified request per key id. The data-plane team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Latency through the signer stayed under 3ms at p99 across the reconciliation replay.

## Disputes runbook

The legacy signer peaked at roughly 39k requests per minute on settlement during the last cycle. Initech confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox. D. Achterberg asked whether payouts still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which sre-core own.

## Globex update

The identity team want the evidence files kept for 7 days after cutover. T. Bergstrom will rerun the webhooks replay once Contoso finish their client release. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## Onboarding queue

M. Lindqvist reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-10-07. Requests with a body over 4096 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Header count per request on payouts is between 24 and 11 in the sampled traffic.

## Evidence retention

P. Oyelaran will rerun the onboarding replay once Umbrella finish their client release. Evidence for disputes is written to the spool directory and collected every 9 minutes. A. Nakamura asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the orders dashboard.

## Reconciliation queue

T. Bergstrom raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Capacity headroom on payouts is about 56 percent at the current peak. The access log truncates query strings longer than 1024 bytes. The request itself is not truncated.

## Dashboards

Disk on gw-edge-02 was at 24 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The partner-integrations team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. L. Fontaine asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard.

## Globex sandbox

Requests with a body over 2048 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Capacity headroom on disputes is about 39 percent at the current peak. The payments-api team asked for one more dry run on gw-edge-02 before disputes moves.

## Catalog replay results

The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The signer account on gw-edge-02 has no outbound network route, which billing verified again on 2025-10-07. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 28k requests per minute on refunds during the last cycle.

## Umbrella update

The payments-api team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. The key directory on gw-edge-01 is readable by the signer accounts only. Latency through the signer stayed under 6ms at p99 across the webhooks replay. Northwind use the same key id for disputes and onboarding. That is allowed. The rollback rehearsal for disputes took 55 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03.

## Globex sandbox

Header count per request on settlement is between 34 and 15 in the sampled traffic. The signer account on gw-edge-02 has no outbound network route, which edge-platform verified again on 2025-11-18. The refunds queue drained in 15 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

## Settlement replay results

The disputes dashboard now splits signature mismatches by key id and by partner. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. Disk on gw-edge-03 was at 65 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. The batch reader on gw-edge-03 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

## Key rotation

`gw-prod-03` was cut on 2025-11-27 and its file is in the key directory on every edge host. The export signer has been on it since 2025-11-28. For inbound request signing, moving to it is a separate change with its own window in the first quarter and is not part of this cutover.

## Rollback rehearsal

Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which billing own. Alert thresholds for catalog stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Requests with a body over 1024 bytes are rejected upstream of the signer and never reach it. Contoso asked for a second sandbox key id and were pointed at the onboarding form.

## Ledger replay results

The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. The signer account on gw-edge-04 has no outbound network route, which identity verified again on 2025-10-14. The rollback rehearsal for webhooks took 25 minutes end to end on gw-edge-03. The fraud-ops team want the evidence files kept for 90 days after cutover. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on disputes is between 16 and 16 in the sampled traffic. J. Delacroix raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. Umbrella confirmed they are on SDK 3.1 in production and 3.2 in their sandbox.

The rollback rehearsal for settlement took 10 minutes end to end on gw-edge-04. The batch reader on gw-edge-04 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file. Capacity headroom on disputes is about 40 percent at the current peak. P. Oyelaran checked that the same refunds request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-04 and gw-edge-01. P. Oyelaran asked whether disputes still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Disk on gw-edge-03 was at 57 percent after the replay and was cleared by hand.

Capacity headroom on refunds is about 30 percent at the current peak. Evidence for orders is written to the spool directory and collected every 50 minutes.

02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md-179-Each session minutes what was agreed, per signer. The register is left as it is. Where minutes turn out to be wrong they are corrected at a later session, in an item that begins "Correction to the minutes of", and the correction is what counts. An item that brings one signer in line with another copies the other's rule as it stood on that day; it does not follow what the other signer does afterwards. An item agreed as effective with a release takes effect on the day that release becomes generally available, and the release calendar has those dates.

# Appendix - Release Calendar

General availability dates for the client libraries and components the signers depend on. A change minuted as effective with a release takes effect on that release's date.

## Host gw-edge-04

Latency through the signer stayed under 5ms at p99 across the disputes replay. The partner-integrations team want the evidence files kept for 30 days after cutover. M. Lindqvist reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-12-02. Alert thresholds for webhooks stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed.

## Host gw-edge-03

Contoso reported 37 failed requests on 2025-10-07, all traced to an expired sandbox credential on their side. T. Bergstrom checked that the same refunds request produces the same canonical hash on gw-edge-01 and gw-edge-03. The access log truncates query strings longer than 2048 bytes. The request itself is not truncated. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. A Umbrella engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards.

## Evidence retention

P. Oyelaran reported that the catalog cutover is on track for the week of 2025-12-02. The partner-integrations team asked that query parameters carrying account numbers be masked in the dashboards. Header count per request on ledger is between 5 and 10 in the sampled traffic. Evidence for payouts is written to the spool directory and collected every 29 minutes.

## Load test

Alert thresholds for reconciliation stay where they are until 2 clean weeks have passed. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. S. Varga asked whether disputes still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. The catalog queue drained in 54 minutes after the replay, which is within the agreed window.

- receiver kit 2.0: general availability 2025-11-28.

- admin CLI 2.2: general availability 2026-02-03.

- export client 1.4: general availability 2025-12-18.

## Umbrella update

M. Lindqvist asked whether onboarding still needs the old batch window. Nobody objected to dropping it. Key files are distributed by the provisioning job, which data-plane own. T. Bergstrom reported that the webhooks cutover is on track for the week of 2025-11-18. The key directory on gw-edge-03 is readable by the signer accounts only. J. Delacroix asked for the canonical hash to be shown next to each mismatch in the webhooks dashboard.

- SDK 3.3: general availability 2026-01-13.

## SDK rollout

Header count per request on settlement is between 21 and 14 in the sampled traffic. A Contoso engineer joined for this item and dropped off afterwards. The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

## Access and accounts

Umbrella use the same key id for ledger and orders. That is allowed. The edge-platform team want the evidence files kept for 14 days after cutover. R. Okonkwo raised that the catalog runbook still names the Perl script. To be fixed after cutover. The legacy signer peaked at roughly 27k requests per minute on disputes during the last cycle. The batch reader on gw-edge-02 tolerates a trailing newline at the end of the input file.

[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Signed header set
D. Achterberg raised that a header outside the signed set can be changed in transit without anyone noticing. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: the `x-ms-*` header family and `content-type` are signed, and nothing else. A. Nakamura will confirm with the partners affected.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## String terminator
D. Achterberg compared the design doc line by line with what the signer hands to HMAC. Agreed: for the export signer, the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. The current client release already behaves this way.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Header values
Northwind reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for BX-HMAC-SHA256 spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. The client libraries follow in their next release.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Query ordering
Umbrella reported intermittent mismatches on requests that repeat a parameter name. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: query parameters are ordered by name only, and parameters that share a name keep the order they arrived in. No change for anyone else.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Body hash
M. Lindqvist asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. P. Oyelaran proposed, and the room agreed, that for MS-HMAC-SHA256 the body-hash field is always the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the body bytes, and a request with no body is treated as a body of zero length. The current client release already behaves this way.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Name list separator
Umbrella asked how the signed header names are separated. R. Okonkwo proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer the signed header names are joined with `,`. K. Mwangi will confirm with the partners affected.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Key id matching
Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Decision for BX-HMAC-SHA256: the key id is matched exactly as sent. Documented in the client notes the same day.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Body hash
S. Varga asked what the body-hash field holds when there is nothing to hash. Agreed: for the webhook signer, a request with no body at all puts the token `EMPTY` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. Effective from this meeting.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Parameters with no value
S. Varga raised parameters that arrive without an equals sign. Decision for outbound webhook signing: a query parameter with no `=` is written with a trailing `=`. Effective from this meeting.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Empty bodies
K. Mwangi asked what counts as an empty body. The old signer could not tell a missing body from a zero length one; the new record format can. Agreed: for the export signer, a request with no body at all puts the token `NONE` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. The client libraries follow in their next release.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Escapes in the target
S. Varga raised that 2 client libraries emit lowercase percent escapes and the fronting proxy might be rewriting them. S. Varga proposed, and the room agreed, that for the export signer the hex digits of every percent escape in the path and the query are uppercased before signing. Effective from this meeting.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Key ids
Northwind's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. D. Achterberg proposed, and the room agreed, that for outbound webhook signing the key id is matched exactly as sent. R. Okonkwo will confirm with the partners affected.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## End of the string to sign
The last byte of the string to sign was questioned by D. Achterberg. Agreed: for AD-HMAC-SHA256, the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. Effective from this meeting.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Key id matching
Umbrella's integration upper-cases every header value it controls, key ids included. Decision for service mesh signing: the key id is matched exactly as sent. S. Varga will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Path handling
Globex's router emits targets such as `/v2/./orders` and their signatures fail whenever something in between tidies the path. Agreed: for batch manifest signing, dot segments in the path are collapsed before signing. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Parameters with no value
Globex's client writes a parameter that has no value as the bare name. Agreed: for the export signer, a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. K. Mwangi will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Header values
Contoso reported mismatches on requests whose header values carry runs of spaces. Agreed: for MS-HMAC-SHA256, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. A. Nakamura will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Key loading
Key file handling came up during the rotation rehearsal. Agreed: for the export signer, the key file is used whole, line ending included. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Header value spacing
Contoso's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. K. Mwangi proposed, and the room agreed, that for the webhook signer header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Key id matching
P. Oyelaran raised key ids that arrive in the wrong case. M. Lindqvist proposed, and the room agreed, that for the admin signer the key id is matched exactly as sent. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Header values
Globex's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Decision for the admin signer: header values go into the header block exactly as received, byte for byte. No change for anyone else.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Scope
4 signers besides the one being migrated come up in these sessions, because they share the Perl tree and most of the people. The notes use these names. Inbound request signing, also written as partner request signing, the gateway request scheme or by its identifier GW-HMAC-SHA256, covers requests partners send to the gateway; it is the only one being migrated and the only one the register describes. Outbound webhook signing, also the webhook signer or callback signing, WH-HMAC-SHA256, covers webhook deliveries we send to partners. Export manifest signing, also the export signer or batch manifest signing, BX-HMAC-SHA256, covers the manifest requests of the nightly settlement export. Service mesh signing, also the mesh signer or internal service signing, MS-HMAC-SHA256, covers calls between our own services. Admin API signing, also the admin signer or ops tooling signing, AD-HMAC-SHA256, covers requests from ops tooling to the admin API. A decision minuted for one of them is a decision for that one only.
[02-2025-09-30-kickoff.md] ## Escapes in the target
P. Oyelaran asked whether percent escapes survive the fronting proxy unchanged. Agreed: for callback signing, percent escapes in the path and the query are signed in the case they arrive in. The current client release already behaves this way.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Valueless parameters
Initech's client writes a parameter that has no value as the bare name. Contoso asked that for the webhook signer a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. Not adopted. The cost of changing every client is not worth it.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Valueless parameters
S. Varga asked what the canonical query does with a name that has no value. Decision for MS-HMAC-SHA256: a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. No change for anyone else.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## String terminator
A. Nakamura found that the line break shown after the last field in the design doc was an artefact of how the example had been pasted. Decision for export manifest signing: the string to sign ends at the last character of the last field, with nothing after it. T. Bergstrom will update the client notes.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## String terminator
The last byte of the string to sign was questioned by D. Achterberg. Decision for internal service signing: the string to sign ends with a line feed after the last field. The current client release already behaves this way.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Signed header set
The signed set came up while preparing the threat review. L. Fontaine proposed, and the room agreed, that for AD-HMAC-SHA256 `host`, `content-type` and the `x-ad-*` family are signed, and nothing else. K. Mwangi will update the client notes.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Which headers are signed
Contoso asked which headers a signature actually covers. Decision for export manifest signing: every header on the request is signed, whatever its name, except `authorization`. The client libraries follow in their next release.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Query ordering
K. Mwangi traced the intermittent mismatches on the nightly export to repeated parameter names. Past the load balancer the order of repeated parameters is no longer the order the client sent. Decision for BX-HMAC-SHA256: query parameters are ordered by name only, and parameters that share a name keep the order they arrived in. Documented in the client notes the same day.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Header values
Umbrella's client pads some header values and the 2 sides end up hashing different bytes. Agreed: for the admin signer, spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and every run of spaces and tabs inside it is collapsed to a single space. No change for anyone else.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Name list separator
S. Varga would like the SDKs to share the code that builds the signed name list. Decision for the admin signer: the signed header names are joined with `,`. No change for anyone else.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Body hash
Debugging around the empty-body token has cost more than the token ever saved. M. Lindqvist proposed that for MS-HMAC-SHA256 a request with no body at all puts the token `NOBODY` in the body-hash field, and a body of zero length is hashed like any other body. Parked until there are numbers to look at; nothing changes for now.
[03-2025-10-07-scope.md] ## Path handling
Initech's router emits targets such as `/v2/./orders` and their signatures fail whenever something in between tidies the path. J. Every request rejected after a change on their side. The request never reached us. Their egress firewall was dropping it. Closed.
[25-partner-support-escalations.md] ## 2025-10-03 Contoso
Every request rejected after a change on their side. They were sending the sandbox key id to the production host. Closed with no change on our side.
[25-partner-support-escalations.md] ## 2025-10-16 Northwind
Every request rejected after a change on their side. The request never reached us. Their egress firewall was dropping it. Closed.

Signatures failing on some of their inbound requests. Support advised that for the gateway request scheme spaces and tabs are stripped from each end of every header value and the inside of the value is left as it is. Resolved.
[25-partner-support-escalations.md] ## 2025-10-24 Contoso
Export manifests failing verification on their side. Support advised that for the export signer a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. Resolved.

Admin API calls from their tooling rejected. Support advised that for admin API signing a request whose body is empty or absent puts the token `BLANK` in the body-hash field. Resolved.

Every request rejected after a change on their side. A middlebox on their side was rewriting the request after it had been signed. Resolved on their side.
[25-partner-support-escalations.md] ## 2025-11-06 Contoso
Signatures failing on some of their inbound requests. Support advised that for partner request signing a query parameter with no `=` is written as the bare name, with no `=`. Resolved.

steps.message:
The port is finished. `tsc -p /app/tsconfig.json` builds cleanly. I ran it over the sample and wrote the result to `/app/out/evidence.ndjson`. I have no gateway to test against, so I haven't confirmed the signatures are accepted.

The sample gives 3 signed, 5 rejected and none verified:

- **Unknown key id:** one record.
- **Missing key id:** one record.
- **Signature mismatch:** two records. These carry `Authorization` headers that were presumably generated under pre-freeze rules, so a mismatch is expected.
- **Malformed authorization:** one record, with a `Bearer` header.

The dossier says different things for the five signers, and later sessions reverse earlier ones. I kept only the decisions for GW-HMAC-SHA256 (partner request signing) as they stood on 2025-12-09:

- **Header set:** every header is signed except `authorization`. This was conditional on all five partners signing off by 12-05, and the sign-off register shows they did.
- **Header values:** spaces and tabs are stripped from both ends, and runs inside the value collapse to one space. A later "correction" minute moved this decision from the webhook signer to the gateway scheme. A proposal to also lowercase values was declined.
- **Name list:** names are joined with `;`. The `,` version was withdrawn and then corrected away.
- **Query:** parameters sort by name and then by value, compared as raw bytes with nothing decoded. A bare name is written as `name=`.
- **Path:** the path is signed as received, with no dot-segment collapsing. The collapse is only effective with SDK 3.3, which is generally available on 2026-01-13.
- **Percent escapes:** signed in the case they arrive in. The uppercasing was conditional on the proxy rewriting escapes, and the proxy capture shows it doesn't.
- **Body hash:** it is always the SHA-256 of the body, and a missing body counts as zero length. `UNSIGNED` is gone, because SDK 3.2.1 became generally available on 2025-12-01.
- **Terminator:** the canonical string has no trailing LF. The register's GW-052 and GW-009 are superseded.
- **Key id:** matched exactly. The case-insensitive request was declined.

Keys:

- **Roster:** `gw-prod-01` and `gw-prod-02`. The legacy strace and lsof show only those two being opened. `gw-prod-03` is the export signer's key, and moving request signing to it is a separate change planned for Q1.
- **Reading:** the key file is used whole, including its trailing newline, as the strace shows it being read.

I made two judgement calls where the dossier is silent:

- **Empty query pairs:** empty pairs from input like `a=1&&b` are dropped.
- **Duplicate headers:** if a header name repeats, the first occurrence supplies the key id or `Authorization`.

The source has no network client and no network calls.
